utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, The Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, everybody. Today we will continue the cross-examination of Mr. Nikolic by Mr. Karnavas. And we have to finish the cross-examination by Mr. Karnavas by 1.45. And I'm very glad to see that the potential evidence has been translated into English and is distributed to everybody, I believe. I would like to thank the translation office for this translation. Well, it seems that Mr. McCloskey hasn't got the translation yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Good morning, Mr. Nikolic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas, are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Always, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We left off yesterday when we were discussing your involvement as the coordinator in Potocari on the morning of July 12th, 1995. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall that, but it wasn't in the morning. But we were talking about my presence in Potocari and the units in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I stand corrected. You got there around -- between 12.00 and 2.00, as I understand it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, roughly about that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And before going there, according to your testimony, you had a pretty good idea of which units were located in Potocari by that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I clearly understood my tasks, and I spoke about this in my testimony, and that is that the units that were to participate in that operation had already been tasked, and they were already in Potocari. I subsequently learned, that is, once I came there and was working there for the next two days, I learned which units were engaged there, or rather which parts of units were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Was -- the 10th Sabotage Reconnaissance Detachment was there, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I was able to identify, and I did know parts of the 10th Sabotage Reconnaissance Detachment because they had been engaged in Bratunac over the previous few months, so I knew they were also there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you were there to coordinate their tasks among the others as well, were you not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there to coordinate in the operation of removal. And among other things, my task was to coordinate the work of the participants in that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And one of the participants, one of them, was the 10th Reconnaissance Sabotage Detachment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that unit is directly attached to or part of the main staff. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 10th Sabotage Detachment is a unit of the main staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Which is above the Drina Corps, the main staff?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That does not mean above it. It means that it is a unit of the main staff. It means that it is a unit which is under the control in the sense of command and in the professional sense, under the command of one of the administrations of the main staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And with whom did you communicate -- or let me withdraw that. Who was in charge on that particular afternoon or however -- you know, that period of time of the 10th Reconnaissance Sabotage Detachment? Who was in charge of that unit that was there that you needed to coordinate with?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, Mr. Karnavas, who was the commander or leader. I don't know exactly what his title was. I think it was commander of the 10th Sabotage Detachment. I knew who their commander is. Now, who was in charge in that operation to be in command of that unit directly, I've already told you that I didn't know that. I didn't know who was in charge of which unit and who was in command of which unit in Potocari. I know who their commanders are generally, but I did not attend a meeting, if ever there was one, at which assignments were issued, and I didn't meet with the commanders either to be able to know who was in command of those units at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness come closer to the microphones, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The witness or the lawyer?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Both, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I was admonished yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, now, let me just go over some of the units that were there based on your testimony which we can see on the transcript pages of 1689 to 1690. We have -- we talked about the 65th Protection Regiment of the main staff. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The 10th Reconnaissance Sabotage Detachment of the main staff. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The Drina Wolves which were -- were they attached to or were they part of the Zvornik Brigade, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a unit of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it wasn't just any kind of -- it wasn't just an ordinary unit; it was -- were they not highly trained soldiers, a crack unit?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really not qualified to talk about units of another brigade, that is, of the Zvornik Brigade, how trained -- well trained they were is really something I can't comment on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So even today -- well, let me -- so your answer is that you today and as well as back then were unaware of the quality of the Drina Wolves as far as being, you know, a fighting unit, as far as their competence, their capabilities as a fighting unit?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I can express my personal opinion about any unit of the Drina Corps. I can make an assessment of units of the main staff. But I was very specific. I'm not qualified to judge to what extent a unit of that level as a part of the Zvornik Brigade is combat ready, how well trained it is. I cannot say because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether they participated on the attack on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard, and this was later confirmed and subsequent information indicates that the Drina Wolves did participate in the attack on Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, there were also various police units, were there not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you're asking me about Potocari or are you asking me generally? Are you asking me about the operation or about Potocari on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, until we move to another segment, to another chapter, we're going to be focussing on Potocari, and we're going to be on the 12th, and we're talking about when you went there. Okay? That's the focus. Very limited period of time. Now, we know from your testimony that you indicated that there were police units with German shepherds. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We know that you saw Stalin there, right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Stalin is Mr. Jevic, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Dusko Jevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He got his nickname because he was a tough instructor in the police academy, right? That's why they call him Stalin?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know why he acquired that name. But I do know that that is how they called him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you knew of him from before? You knew him personally?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, superficially, nothing special. We never socialised. Before that, we were never assigned to the same task, but I did know him as a member of the MUP. So extremely superficially and by sight, but it can be said that I did know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what was his rank?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what the structure of the police was, what their ranks are, what their duties were. Except for Borovcanin and Savic, I'm not familiar with their structure or their positions in the special brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it you were not familiar with the structure back then as well, on that particular day? If you're not today, it stands to reason that you wouldn't be back then, right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It stands to reason that one could conclude that I just knew that they belonged to a special MUP brigade, and I knew under whose direct command they were. I know that the direct commanding officer of those units was Ljubisa Borovcanin. He was in charge of them. And I knew that the units that were in Potocari under Bjelic's command belonged to the unit under the command of Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. What rank was Mr. Borovcanin, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I knew and according to what he himself said, I think he had the rank of a police colonel. I may be wrong. But I think that he represented himself as a colonel. Whether that is true or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So just so I can be sure about this, and perhaps others may be interested as well, at that particular time, you, Momir Nikolic, or Captain Nikolic, chief of intelligence and security, was not sure whether Mr. Borovcanin was indeed a colonel in the MUP? Is that your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I said what I thought. I think that at the time he was a colonel. Now, whether he was a colonel, a lieutenant-colonel, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that is my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Now, those units, those MUP units under Mr. Borovcanin, they were his subordinates, were they not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And from listening to your testimony and reading your statements, it doesn't appear anywhere that Captain Nikolic contacted Colonel Borovcanin to find out what, if any, instructions he had given his units that were located in Potocari at the time that you arrived, around noon, or slightly thereafter, on July 12th, 1995. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I never stated, and I am still saying now, that I did not meet with Mr. Borovcanin because Mr. Borovcanin is a commander, and he communicates with officers from the command structure. And all I can do with respect to Mr. Borovcanin is to provide a service to him, that is, give him intelligence information along the axis of his combat operations. So with respect to intelligence, I can communicate with him and fulfill my duties and obligations. Outside of that, I had no need, nor is it my duty for me to sit and talk to commanders about anything. So Mr. Borovcanin has the right and the competence and obligation to communicate and discuss and agree on assignments at the command level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So it would be fair to say that when you went to Potocari, or before going to Potocari, just so I'm clear about this, you never spoke with any of the commanders of the units that were located in Potocari. This is before going there.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can't be put that way because I did speak to Borovcanin, and I said that in my testimony. So I spoke to him on one occasion, a day prior to my going to Potocari. But in connection with the assignments, intelligence information, and providing intelligence information to the commander in person, for him to be able to use armoured forces, to use a tank to hit targets that are defined as tanks -- as targets with which armoured units, should be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt the witness. We're talking about a particular time and place. We're not talking about the 11th, we're talking about the 12th. So focus, work with me on the 12th. Prior to going to Potocari, you never spoke with any of the commanders of any of the units that you were there to coordinate with. Isn't that a fact? And I'm specifically directing my question with respect to your tasks of coordination in Potocari on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, the answer is no. That is, I did not speak to any unit commander of the units engaged in Potocari at the time. But before that, you asked me if I had ever spoken to the commander, and I answered yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I apologise if there was a misunderstanding. You did ask me whether I had ever spoken to him, and I said that I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You've answered the question. Now, when got to Potocari, is it not a fact that you never spoke while you were in Potocari before you began your coordination, the tasks that were given to you by Colonel Jankovic, you never spoke there with the commanders of the various units that you were there to coordinate? Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, I indicated precisely with whom I spoke. There are certain things I was not asked about, and about which I can talk now --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you again. The question was very specific. The question was very specific. You don't understand it, ask me. I'll rephrase it. When you got to Potocari on the 12th, all right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You were there to coordinate units by your own testimony. Those units had commanders. While you were there, is it not a fact that you never contacted the commanders of those units with respect to your tasks for coordination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Object. In that leading question is a misstatement of the previous testimony, that is an improper way to ask a leading question. This witness clearly said he spoke to Dusko Jevic, the commander of the special police. The question has a misstatement of fact. That's an improper question. And it's objectionable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may -- let me respond for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no. Well, Mr. McCloskey, I think you know the Defence counsel has the right to check the testimony given by this witness in the direct. But on the other hand, on the other hand, Mr. Karnavas, you may quote what he said in the direct or in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me be a little more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the commanders of the units, the immediate commanders that were commanding the units on the ground in Potocari. I'm talking about their commanders such as, for instance, Borovcanin, such as -- well, if the Drina Wolves were under the Zvornik Brigade, it would be Pandurevic, right? That's what I'm talking about. So my question to you, sir, is when you went to Potocari, when you were there, you did not contact any of those commanders?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. Karnavas. The way you're putting the question, I did not contact any of those supreme commanders, commanders of special brigades of MUP. No, I did not. I say "supreme" in inverted commas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, another very specific question: Did you contact each and every commander of the units - not the supreme now, but of the units that were there in Potocari - did you contact each and every one of them to find out what their individual tasks were in accordance to what they had been tasked by their superior commands?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, that was absolutely impossible. And if you want that kind of answer, then no, I didn't contact individually each of those participants to ask them what tasks they had been assigned. I did not contact them. I knew what was supposed to be done that day, Mr. Karnavas. That means I knew, I knew we had to evacuate 30.000 people. I also knew my role in that operation. I also knew that up there in that place, Potocari, units had been brought in to do the job. Now, individually, who had received what assignment from their commanders, that, I did not know, but I did tour the region in its entirety. I saw the units present, in place there. And when the operation started, wherever there were problems, I solved them in the way I saw fit. So there's absolutely nothing unclear on that score. Now, Your Honours, I have to add something, please. Had there been a plan, Mr. Karnavas, I know what you want to hear from me, I know what you want to get --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Object. It goes beyond the scope of my question. I'd like to use my time as efficiently as possible. He can certainly say what he wishes through Mr. McCloskey. But this goes beyond the scope of my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, if you want to provide more information, I believe that the counsel will ask you questions. Here is a question and answer procedure. And counsel has the duty to lead you to the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, the definition of "coordination" as I understand it is to synchronise the aim, the place, the time, and the means of the various units that you were supposed to be coordinating. Would you agree or disagree with that definition of what coordination means under the circumstances that we are discussing here today in this Tribunal? Aim, place, time, means, all these units in a very confined area, we're talking about 30.000 people, mass chaos, humanitarian crisis.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a theoretical definition, and it's just theory, what you've just said. All I can do is to tell you how I understood this coordination, and I understood it in the following way: I was given my assignment, my tasks, within the frameworks of my overall assignment, within the frameworks of the overall operation of moving the inhabitants of Potocari to Kladanj and further afield, elsewhere. To coordinate, to guide, because I was from Bratunac myself, I was an officer from the region, to guide the work of those units to resolve certain problems that might crop up that I come across during that operation. Furthermore, to make suggestions and proposals, and if necessary to issue orders in the sense of having the main say as to what will be done when and where, in the technical sense, in the organisational sense, et cetera. That was my understanding of it. Now, what you just said is an exact definition, yes, it is theory, the theory concerning coordination, governing coordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Nikolic, yesterday I asked whether you had received some sort of letter of introduction from Colonel Jankovic so you could show to the various commanders or even soldiers from the various units who you were and what powers or mandate you had in order to guide them and, if necessary, order them around. I believe the answer was no letter of introduction was given to you by Colonel Jankovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. My answer was that no letter except an oral order did I receive from Colonel Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And no written order, no formal written order was given to you with, perhaps, a signature and a stamp that would have the value and the weight of an official order was given to you by Colonel Jankovic so you could show it around just in case one of these higher ranking officers, like, say, a major or lieutenant-colonel or a colonel, all of these ranks who were there at the time leading units, you didn't have an official document to show where your power came from in ordering them or their troops around in this highly regimented system called army where rank is rather important as to who gives the orders and who takes the orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, it's a statement, not a question. I think, you know, it's a reasonable suspicion on this issue, but you have to put it in the form of a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase. I was -- I was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You did not get an order, an official order from Colonel Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received an official order. I did receive an official order from Colonel Jankovic, and that order, let me just finish, please, Mr. Karnavas, was not in written form. I received an oral order from Colonel Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But nobody was there to hear that oral order, so how could these people back -- these higher ranking officers or the foot soldiers of the various units in Potocari at this time know that you had this order, this oral order if nobody was there to hear it, to witness it, to verify it? How?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, that's not my fault. I'm telling you the form the order took and that I was given. Now, why there was nobody else there, that's not my problem, and I can't influence that. I can do nothing about that. I told you where I got the order, who I got the order from, and what kind of order it was. The fact that there was nobody else there is not my problem. So I really can't have any influence on that. There's nothing I can do about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All these units had already got their orders, and they knew what they were going to be doing. You know, you had these colonels or these majors out there. They had their orders. Why was it necessary to have Captain Nikolic go there? They already had their orders. Why did they need you there, especially if -- especially if - help you out here a bit - especially if you never went to speak to any of them to find out what their individual tasks were? Help me out.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't help you out, Mr. Karnavas, on that point. I told you what I knew. Now, why it was the way it was, I really don't know. I don't know the details surrounding all that. All I know is my role and what I received. Now, why it was done in that way, I really can't say. Who ordered it that way, I don't know that either because I didn't attend any of the meetings. I don't know that part of it, who issued an order of that kind. I don't know who issued any of the other orders and compiled a list of participants there. I don't know that either because nobody told me officially because I never attended official meetings of that type. So what I'm telling you is what I know. Now, whether that was the right way to go about it, I can give you my comments here and now. But in answer to your question, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you went back on the 13th, right? On the 13th -- I'm switching, I'm sorry. Now let's talk about the 13th of July, next day. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Different chapter. On the 13th, you went back to Potocari. Right? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you went back because the task that you had been ordered, according to you, by Colonel Jankovic had not been completed. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, this is another misstatement of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to object, Your Honour, to coaching the witness as to what to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm not going to say it, but I think the world knows what he said on that point, and that is a misstatement. It's fundamental for a lawyer in his position not to misstate the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I believe that you have to rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the 13th, was your task completed, the one that was given to you by Jankovic? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 13th, it was not completed, or rather the operation was not completed of this removal, nor was my task around the coordination at Potocari completed either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, you said as much in the transcript. And having been accused by the Prosecutor, let me point him out to page 1709.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I stipulate that his job wasn't done. They had a lot more people to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There was no need for the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, there's no need for the objection because the Defence counsel is just going to quote what he said in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you went back on the 13th, you only stayed there an hour or an hour and a half. Isn't that correct? Is that correct, on the 13th, now?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I said during my previous testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, from page 709: "How long were you there on this visit to Potocari on the 13th"? Question posed by Mr. McCloskey. Answer: "I was in Potocari only very briefly on the 13th. So on the whole, this lasted for one hour at most, perhaps a little longer, after which I went back to the headquarters or rather the military police building where the military police were stationed." Now, when you went there in the morning, had the evacuation been completed of everyone that you were there to coordinate?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. The evacuation continued on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that was still part of your mandate, was it not, for you to be coordinating the evacuation? Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one of the tasks was that one, too, on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that was a continuing task that had been given to you according to your testimony and what you told the Prosecutor, that was the task given to you earlier that day, and that task had not been completed. And according to you, that was an order. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question contains a number of observations and questions as well. Now, the evacuation on the 13th was not completed, no. My task continued on the 13th to coordinate along those assignments in Potocari. And the third question that you asked me, the order -- or rather, I received no order on the 12th in written form, in writing. I received an order orally from Colonel Jankovic for that particular task.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that order was still in effect on the 13th because you hadn't completed it.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could put it that way because after this order from Colonel Jankovic, I didn't receive any others, if you mean Colonel Jankovic, if that's who you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, not quite. Would it not be fair to say that when you're given an order, you have to carry it all the way through to its full completion unless you're interrupted with another order?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in principle, you could put it that way. That is to say, the orders one receives, until the task is completed, you go on. Or until you receive another order. So it is a task which should be completed within the frameworks of the initial order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So there was no need for you to ask Colonel Blagojevic on the 13th whether you could go to Potocari and continue the task that you had already been given, according to what you say, by the main staff. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not right, Mr. Karnavas. After the first day, I informed Blagojevic as to where I was. On the 12th, I was the duty officer. And during that evening, I informed Colonel Blagojevic of what I was engaged on, so I saw Blagojevic on the 12th. I saw Colonel Blagojevic on the 13th, too, in the morning when I arrived. Colonel Blagojevic knew about the operation to shift these 30.000 people, and Colonel Blagojevic did not by a single gesture or order or in any other way question, prohibit, or stop me in any way to go about my business in Potocari the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, when you went to Potocari on the 12th, I take it you drove there. You had your own car. I believe the colour was blue, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was blue or some other colour. There were several cars in the police that I used. There was a Golf, one Golf, another Golf, blue. There was a Zastava-type car. I really can't say which one that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was your car there handy by the Hotel Fontana when you left for Potocari? Because we know you never went to the headquarters to see your commander. Was your car there?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I always had my car handy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you go to Potocari with anyone in particular, or did you just go by yourself? When you went to coordinate.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Potocari alone on the 12th. And as far as I remember, in Potocari, I was joined by another -- by some policemen from the Bratunac Brigade, one policeman. I think his name was Nenad Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I have a statement here from Nenad Jokic. Let's see what he has to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could provide everybody with a copy. I guess we need to give this an identification number, unless it has one. I believe we're up to 39, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me show you what has been marked for identification purposes as D39/1. And I believe you have been focussed to a particular page. It's page 4. But for the record, your page should read 13070M, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for everyone else's convenience, if you could turn to page L0089853, and I'll be going through that page and the following page. And starting with around line 10, to focus everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So if you could read page 4, sir. And I believe we've already marked it for you for your convenience.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's read it. On line 10, it says: "So I was in Bratunac" -- he's being questioned by Peter McCloskey. "So I was in Bratunac, and later we were given the order to go to Potocari." Peter McCloskey: "Who gave you the order?" Mr. Jokic: "I accompanied Momir Nikolic." Mr. McCloskey: "What order did Momir Nikolic give you?" "To me?" Peter McCloskey: "To you or to others that you witnessed." Mr. Jokic: "I was alone with him." Peter McCloskey: "Were you normally his escort in those days?" And then Jokic: "I asked him whether it was safe to go there." Peter McCloskey: "Were you normally his escort in those days on the 12th and the 13th?" Mr. Jokic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This could go on forever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I want to read the appropriate part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We've all read it. If we could get a question on a particular point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I want to give context to this, and I'm entitled to use my time in a proper fashion. This is proper. I want to give the gentleman an opportunity to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since this paragraph is not that long, you may continue, Mr. Karnavas. But later on, I don't think it's necessary to read the whole page because everybody has got a copy, also the witness also got one. You just draw his attention to certain particular places. Then ask your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So the question was "were you normally his escort in those days on the 12th and 13th?" That's what I just read before the objection. Line 20 on this particular page. "That happened by accident because he came to the military police office, and he said he wanted somebody to accompany him." "Okay. And how come he ended with you?" "I was there." "What did you hear Momir Nikolic, what did Momir Nikolic say to you as you went together to Potocari?" "He did say nothing in particular. We talked about... " "And so where did you go and who did Momir Nikolic see when you went to Potocari?" "So we came to Potocari near the UNPROFOR camp and that factory." "About what time of day was this? Just roughly." "I can't exactly remember, I think it was like 11.00, maybe later." And then there's a conversation about the Hotel Fontana. He's pressed. He's not sure whether he was there on the 11th or the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record, the Prosecution has moved to have this transcript come in through Rule 92 bis. And of course, I'll be making a request for the gentleman to be appearing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Nikolic, it would appear, would it not, at least from what this gentleman says that on that day, somewhere around 11.00, you went to the Bratunac Police Station, which is located by your testimony and from what we all know approximate by 2 minutes from the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, directly in front of it, you went there, picked him up, and together the two of you, not alone, the two of you went to Potocari. Does that not appear from this statement or from this questioning statement, where Mr. McCloskey was questioning Mr. Jokic? Does it not say that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, that comes from the statement made by Mr. Jokic. One could deduce that. But that is absolutely not correct. Mr. Jokic was there on the 12th at 10.00 as security at the entrance to the Fontana Hotel. He was not at the police station at that time. So the meeting began at 10.00 and lasted -- well, I don't know exactly how long it lasted. And you can see Mr. Jokic on the footage, on a picture providing physical security of the Fontana Hotel. So you can see him at the entrance to the Hotel Fontana. And it's not true according to his statement that he was at the police station. He was on duty in front of the Fontana Hotel providing security as a security detail for the Fontana Hotel, and you'll be able to see that that is so if you look at the videotape that the Prosecution provided to you and to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are you also denying having him in the car with you as you drove to Potocari on that particular morning? Would you like to retract your earlier statement that you went alone and maybe --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. Karnavas. I do not wish to retract my statement. I went to Potocari alone. He came to Potocari as far as I can remember in his own car, not in my car with me. That is the truth. And Jokic was with me in Potocari in the role of some sort of security or escort for me. So that is the truth with respect to this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Who ordered you to go to Colonel Franken - I believe he was a major back then - to collect the rent? This was, I believe, on the -- around the 14th or 15th of July. Let me back up. Let me back up. Do you know who Major Franken is?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Franken, I think I do know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He was at DutchBat, was he not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall going to see him, going there and asking for rent, for rent, rent money, either for the DutchBat or for the UNMO, the observers, the United Nations Military Observers. Do you recall doing that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know, Mr. Karnavas, what you're talking about. What rent? To whom? What?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So it doesn't ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't mean anything to me, that I went to take rent from Franken? That really and absolutely -- first of all, the Dutch Battalion was based, headquartered in Potocari. They didn't pay any rent. They didn't pay anything to anyone. They didn't have any obligation to do so, nor did I have anything to do with any rent. It was a base, a factory. I really don't know what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about for housing the prisoners or the refugees? Did you try to collect rent for that, or rent for the United Nations Military Observers? Do you ever recall going there, trying to have a meeting with him, and asking him to give you, I guess on behalf of the -- well, whoever you were representing, rent money?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Karnavas, I really cannot understand what you're saying. First of all, I can't understand that you're asking any such thing, not to mention anything more. The Dutch Battalion had nothing to do with any kind of housing, and never did they pay anything as far as I know. Everything linked to the Dutch Battalion and everything that was done with them was done through official enterprises and organs. If you are alluding to something else, another event, please tell me so I know what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, did you ever contact him with a bill -- you were going to present him with a bill for the building that was rented by the United Nations Military Observers, the UNMO?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which building were they renting, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this, Mr. Nikolic: Do you ever recall going there, driving a Toyota, approaching him, asking to collect rent? Yes or no. Pretty simple.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, that really is a ridiculous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me turn everyone's attention to the transcript from Colonel Franken. This is on September 15, 2003. And I will start with page 1557.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could get copies of that so I can see it in the proper context and so we know what's being talked about. I unfortunately wasn't here during that testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may read the relevant part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's pretty short, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I was doing the questioning, by the way. "Did you see Nikolic around that time, the 12th or 13th?" This is page 1557, line 22, starting with line 22. Answer -- I'm sorry, that was line 24. Answer: "No. The first time I saw Nikolic was I think on the 14th afternoon or the 15th when he came to the camp by car." "Okay. Did you have a conversation with him since you already knew him, or did you just see him and then you went about your business?" Answer, line 4: "No, he came not on some kind of a visit. He came with a purpose, and I believe on that occasion, he came in with the car of our former technician. On the occasion of - what was it? - the bill for the building the UNMO rented had to be paid, and he tried to have DutchBat pay for the cost of made by the Bosnian Serb army for the POWs." Question: "Did he inform you who had instructed him or was he there --" "No, no, he announced that he came. He asked that he could come on the base with his car. I allowed him that. So he parked it in front of the HQ, the headquarters, and then we spoke about this." "And did he ask you, did he throw a particular figure at you, how much the rent was?" "No, it didn't come that far. As far as the UNMO were concerned, I told you before, they were not -- they didn't belong to DutchBat. So I said, okay, I'll have the UNMO make contact with you about that thing, and I told him that it's absolutely ridiculous let me pay for POWs they took, and he didn't insist further on. So I never heard the math." "Okay. Do you know whether he wanted cheque, cash, credit card?" "The discussion didn't come that far." "Okay. And as far as you know or as far as you recollect, he didn't say I have been ordered by Mladic?" "No." And then he goes on, he says: "He just showed up." And I just read all the way to page 1559. Now, do you recall that occasion, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you have read, Mr. Karnavas, never happened. And I never had any obligation or duty to ask for any kind of rent. The only thing that is possible, the only possibility is -- but I'm not sure of that. I don't know whether anyone was in Fontana at the time. At the Fontana Hotel, I think military observers were present for a time, and they had a contract with the Fontana Hotel. They slept there, the observers and their interpreter Petar Uscumlic had a contract with the hotel and they paid rent to the hotel. The agreement was on an individual basis and had nothing to do with me. I never asked anything like that of Mr. Franken, nor did I discuss any such thing with him. As for the prisoners and their status and payment for them, absolutely not, except for the physical security of the prisoners by the Dutch Battalion, I had nothing to do with their stay there, their status, their departure from there or anything else in that connection. So Mr. Karnavas, that simply does not stand. I was never implicated in any such activity, nor did I ask him for anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And since this didn't happen, according to you, I take it you never went there with a blue Japanese car that belonged to one of their technicians who just happened to be -- his name is Rizo. And he just happened to be Muslim. That didn't happen either?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas, I didn't say that. I did drive after the fall of the Srebrenica enclave, I did for a while drive a blue car that was seized from Mr. Rizo. So he handed me the keys, or rather, one of his workers, a policeman from the Bratunac Brigade - you can take a statement from him. So Rizo gave him the keys voluntarily. This policeman gave the keys to me. After that, I drove it for a while, and then this blue car was requisitioned for the needs of the Bratunac Brigade. And this blue car drove Commander Blagojevic personally. After that, this blue car, when Commander Blagojevic left the Bratunac Brigade --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me. The question was on that particular day, did you go there with a blue Toyota? That was the question, that belonged to Rizo on that day. Do you recall doing that? I'm not interested in what you did with the car afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think he was answering the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It went well beyond the scope of the question, Your Honour. The question was if he recalls showing up on that particular day trying to collect rent driving the blue Toyota that belonged to Rizo. Yes or no. What he did afterwards on his personal time driving around somebody else's car that he confiscated is of no interest to me unless we're here for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the witness answered that I did drive after the fall of the Srebrenica enclave. I did for a while drive a blue car that was seized from Mr. Rizo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but we have a transcript from Colonel Franken who says in very particular words that he showed up with Rizo in Rizo's car on that particular day. So I'm merely trying to help him out. He doesn't have a recollection of asking for the bill. I would now like to lock him in because either he's misstating the facts or Colonel Franken is misstating the facts. One of the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So if I can focus you back on that particular day that Colonel Franken says he recalls you showing up on the base, on the base, driving a car. You're driving, Rizo is sitting as a passenger in his own blue Toyota that you later confiscate. Do you recall showing up on that particular day over there presenting yourself as a collection agency for rent? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. He's just playing around. It's his time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, put your question in a very simple way, and you added a lot of elements in your question, so it becomes extremely difficult to know where you are going.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Just ask one question. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall showing up with a blue Toyota that belonged to Rizo with Rizo in the car trying to collect rent from Colonel Franken? Major at the time. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. I do not recall that, nor did that happen. That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's time for a break. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Your Honour, because of the way the question was asked, we don't know if he's referring to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I can ask it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- Not meeting with Franken, not driving the car with the guy or all of them. That's the problem with those kind of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We've already established through the gentleman that he doesn't recall ever trying to collect the rent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's right, that's why we didn't need that added to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The question was, the question was now because we have facts from a witness, their witness who says not only did he show up trying to collect the rent, but he showed up with their driver in a blue Toyota. Why is that significant? It's significant because it means that Colonel Franken -- this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a speech making again, Your Honour. I just would like a straight question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm responding to what he's saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There's no need for that because we all know the points. Just ask a simple question about the car, not about collecting rent. Then we'll break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the driving the car ties into collecting of the rent because that's perhaps why Franken -- that's why it was so significant because he was shocked to see Rizo, their employee, in his car being driven by Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, first of all, you asked the question about collecting the rent. The witness denied that fact. It's quite clear. The second should be whether he was there on that particular day in a particular car. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I was looping, Your Honour. I was taking part of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Don't add more elements into one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I apologise. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ever show up and meet with Colonel or Major Franken on the 14th or 15th in Mr. Rizo's blue Toyota?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In that period of time, I know for certain that I did not meet with Mr. Franken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll accept that. I'll accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, before we start, there's a scheduling announcement. This afternoon, we'll start at 3.15 instead of 3.00 sharp. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That doesn't mean I get an extra 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no, you have to finish by 1.45. I promised you the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just thought I'd ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, if we could return -- if we could return to the 12th, as I understand it from your testimony and your statement, that on the afternoon of the 12th or the evening of the 12th, you met with your commander. And at that time, you described the conditions in Potocari on that particular day. Do you recall making -- testifying about that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it seemed to me from listening to you that when you were describing these events to your commander, you sort of -- you were rather disturbed of what you had been seeing in Potocari on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That cannot be seen from my statement. I was just describing the situation. I told him what the situation was like in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you told him it was a hell, right? That the conditions were bad, that mothers were having their children torn away from their hands or their arms, and wives having their husbands separated from them. You told him all of these, and you described how, as I believe from your reading your statement, how the conditions were rather horrendous.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. I said, in fact, that the conditions there were horrendous, that the scenes were horrendous, that the overall situation was extremely difficult. But if I remember correctly, I don't think that I mentioned anywhere that children were being snatched away from their mothers. I don't think I mentioned that. The rest, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now -- so I take it from the way you've described it, you as a man, a father, husband, what you were describing and when you were describing it, you were rather moved, disturbed, at what you had seen that day, were you not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every normal man, Mr. Karnavas, and I consider myself that, would have to have felt moved, and he would necessarily find it difficult to stomach all the ugly things that were happening over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, on that day, on the 12th in the afternoon where those ugly things were happening, were you not, in fact, trying to locate and interrogate wounded refugees? Was that not one of the additional tasks that you -- or burdens shall we call it, that you took upon yourself in addition to the coordination that you were involved with?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. The refugees, and I'm talking about the 12th, or rather, the wounded that you mentioned, and the international forces, the UNPROFOR, the international observers, the military observers, and other international factors that were present in Srebrenica, or rather, in Potocari at the time, were clearly within the terms of reference of Colonel Jankovic. And he told me that my role for that period ceased, that is, my role as a liaison officer, and that all activities linked to those contacts would be taken over by him in the ensuing period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may ask to go into private session for one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me focus your attention back to the 13th, the 13th of July, 1995. As I understand your testimony, at some point you were informed by the military police that General Mladic was going to be going down to Konjevic Polje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That was sometime in the morning, mid-morning of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was after my return from Potocari. That is to say, I stayed in Potocari for a time, and then I came to the building of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's where you found out from them?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's when I was told that on that day, Mladic was, roughly during that period of time actually, or several hours afterwards, was supposed to pass along that route towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so you went down that road to make sure that it was safe. Right? That was your testimony, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went to check the situation out, the safety and security of that line of communication on that day during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You weren't under any orders to do that; that was on your own. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. I did not receive any order. I acted as I thought best at that moment in time, and I made the decision as the security organ in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Kind of interesting that everybody would know where Mladic is coming and going. I mean, if there's a security risk. Don't you find it kind of curious that he would telegraph to everybody: "Here's where I'm going"?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If you're asking me, then quite certainly he didn't inform everybody where he was going. The squad from the Bratunac Brigade was one of the participants in providing security for General Mladic so that it was quite normal for the police to know about his whereabouts and his movements, and there would be one or two units included in the security of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. But we're talking about the police that were with him. When they're with him, obviously they know where he is. The ones that are back in the headquarters aren't necessarily told, "here's where General Mladic is going," so that information is revealed.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to the nature of the job, you couldn't put it that way. They should have had information about General Mladic's movements, the Bratunac Brigade and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, that road was heavily guarded, was it not, already? If you don't know, let us know, but...

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know at that point in time the exact level or degree to which that road was safe when I decided to go out and check it out. But I did, of course, know that some of the police forces were there. That is what I did know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, part of that road had already -- being policed or being secured by the police well before Srebrenica. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know how it was secured, how that part of the road had been secured before the attack on Srebrenica. All I knew was what was going on in Konjevic Polje before the attack on Srebrenica. And I testified about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so you went there, and I take it you took a lot of people with you because you weren't sure how safe this road was. So just in case you got in trouble, you must have taken some backup support when you drove down that road to make sure that it was safe for the general. Did you take any support with you when you were trying to check out the safety of this particular road? Or were you just driving around casually hoping that you didn't get hit by a stray bullet or be ambushed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection again. He's just playing. It's silliness. It's too serious a matter to talk like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, just ask a simple question. Did you take anybody with you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll ask it again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you take anybody with you when you were there to check that piece of road for its safety? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who did you take? How many people?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the way in my car, there was a policeman with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, so it was just you and a police officer driving down this road checking the safety of the road for the supreme commander of the army. That's your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with the policeman, I drove in that direction and along that stretch of road to check out what I was interested in, to see what the security and safety was and the communication lines, how far they were open towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then when you found that it was safe and you had reached the destination, you stayed there waiting for General Mladic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I established that the road was quite safe and that nothing else had to be undertaken, I stayed in Konjevic Polje once I had got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you waited for General Mladic. That was part of the question. You waited for him, right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. Yes, I did. I waited for General Mladic to pass by.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Were you just waiting for him to pass by, or were you waiting to report to him?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, at that point in time, I was waiting for him to pass through Konjevic Polje. I didn't know what he intended to do in Konjevic Polje, whether he intended to stay and ask me anything, whether I would have occasion to report to him. I knew nothing about that at that point in time. I was waiting for him to pass through, to pass through that junction, crossroads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at some point he arrived. Right? At some point --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he did arrive. General Mladic did arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as I understand your testimony, it was you that went to him to report, to give him a report.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I met General Mladic on the asphalt road at the crossroads there when he stepped out of his car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He hadn't given you any particular tasks.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I reported to General Mladic, telling him that everything was all right, in order, that there were no problems. And all the rest he could see for himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And when you asked him what would happen to these people, which you already knew, according to your testimony, and he made that hand movement which you interpreted to mean "they will all be killed," there was no one there to hear you ask that question, was there?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many people round about. Nobody approached, and that's customary of which the reporting, that it is always done at a distance from the person you are reporting to. I think -- I don't think our conversation was within this reporting period. While I was reporting to him, we were standing straight, and I asked him: "General, sir, what should be done with the people next?" And he made the gesture that I described. And that's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it was just you and him having this conversation at the time.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was reporting to him, and then just the two of us continued the conversation about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I guess what I'm trying to make sure that we all understand, there was nobody else there to hear this supposed conversation that took place between you and General Mladic. That's the question. There was no one there to verify that this conversation did, indeed, take place.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, no one could have been in the immediate vicinity of me and General Mladic. I've already told you that around us, there were security people at a distance, which is normal. They weren't close to us. They weren't listening to our conversation. And it is not customary for them to be there. They were at a normal distance. There were several of them, several soldiers who were securing the spot where the two of us were standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I want to focus on a different area. And I want to recall to your attention your testimony with respect to Mr. Petrovic who, I believe, you have indicated on the record was involved in taking revenge for his brother by killing six prisoners that had been captured when you were with him and Mirko Jankovic driving around with the APC. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I recall exactly what I said in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you stand by your testimony today that while you were driving the APC -- while you were in the APC and it was being driven, you came across six prisoners who were later killed by Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I stand by what I said in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely in the way I said it in my statement. And I can repeat that once again. I stand by my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No need to repeat. Okay, if I could share with you what has been marked for identification purposes as Defence Exhibit 37/1, D37/1, and D38/1. And I'm merely interested in you focussing for the moment on the first one, D37, which is a statement, and it is to myself. It's a statement. In other words, we're not dealing with the one given to the Bratunac Police Station, but we're dealing with the one that was given to a Risto Lugonjic and is directed to me. If you could please take a look at it, and first of all, before you go on to read it -- well, why don't you look at it, and we can discuss it.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I have some time to read through this whole statement because it is a very important matter, and I would like to ask you kindly to allow me to read it in its entirety because I have not had occasion to read this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Might I make a suggestion, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why don't we take an early break so he can read it on the break time rather than my time. Because these are -- they're not terribly long, but I don't want to spend 15 minutes standing while he's reading, if I can avoid it. If I can avoid it. I'm just asking. I'm just making a suggestion, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we may have a break. But the next sitting will be a little bit too long. What if we come back at 5 minutes past 12.00. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's okay with me, Your Honour. I'm just trying to be efficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. And by the way, in that private session, you used two documents, and one document we heard is numbered as D40.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about the other?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: D41, Your Honour. D41. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. So we'll resume at 5 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, did you have a chance to read those two documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you had the chance to read the documents during the break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I only received one document, only one statement. And I've read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let us start from that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, is that document the statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry. Let me repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is the document you have in front of you, is that the one that bears my name on it? It's a statement.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in reading -- in reading this document, do you recognise the person who gave the document?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, and who may that be?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Mr. Mile Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is that the same Mile Petrovic that you've testified to before?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the Mile Petrovic that I testified about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in reading the document, I believe it's on the last page, it states that back in March or April, your lawyers went to meet with this gentleman. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just cannot confirm the exact date, whether it was in March or April. But I can confirm that I have information that my lawyers did meet with Mile Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when you say your lawyers, are we speaking of Mr. Londrovic and Mr. Kirsch, and this gentleman Stanko Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I'm not quite sure about that. But I think that Mr. Kirsch was not involved. I think it was Mr. Londrovic and my investigators, that is, the investigators from my team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And would it be fair to say that they went to meet with Mr. Petrovic at your request?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, among others, I mentioned this name, the name of Mile Petrovic, with whom my lawyers could and should talk. And I can confirm that I gave this man's name to my lawyers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And from the date March or April 2003, it would seem to me - correct me if I am wrong - that if you started your negotiations with the Prosecution around November or December, and you didn't reach an agreement until end of April, this encounter of your lawyers with this witness must have been during that critical period, that critical negotiating period. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I can only speculate about that because I don't know exactly. I don't have the date on me as to when they met.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But it was during the period when you were negotiating the facts as to what you would be willing to admit and acknowledge and provide to the Prosecution. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that I don't know. And I can't say any more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I'll move on. Now, in reading this statement, it would appear, would it not, that Mr. Petrovic's account as to what happened is dramatically different from your version? Is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot describe in that way Mr. Petrovic's statement. I can talk about Mr. Petrovic's statement as a whole and point by point. And I would not agree with your description.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, Mr. Petrovic states, on page 1, that they only -- that you picked up two prisoners, not six.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I am claiming here that in that group, there were five or six prisoners, as many as I had said in my testimony and in my first statement. I continue to assert that there were more than two. Five or six to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. In your statement, you do not acknowledge and take responsibility for physically abusing any prisoners by hitting them with the butt of a rifle. But Mr. Petrovic claims that that's what he witnessed. So we have a difference there, don't we?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. That is what Petrovic says in his statement. But I am claiming here that never in my life have I hit anyone with a rifle. Not a single prisoner have I hit or touched or had any physical contact with, never mind hitting anyone with a rifle. Furthermore, to clarify, I did not carry a rifle. In that period of time, I was armed with a pistol in a holster in my belt, CZ69, a pistol I always carried with me. And when I went into the field, again, I didn't carry a rifle. I carried a shorter weapon, an Uzi. So what he said is absolutely not true. I wasn't armed with a rifle, and I didn't have a rifle when I was on that route.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And you never hit anyone, as is described here, with the butt of any weapon? You never abused any prisoners, as described.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. I understand.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. Neither then nor ever during the whole duration of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Petrovic states that he was on top, and not you, and that you were, in fact, in the APC. I take it you dispute that as well.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. Karnavas. I know exactly where I was. Mr. Petrovic was at the weapon, a machine-gun of a high calibre on the APC. I, too, was on the top sitting at the transporter with my legs inside the APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And he also states that there wasn't a megaphone on the APC from which to call the Muslims to come from the hills or from they were hiding. You take exception with that, too?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do deny that, too. I claim, and I said it in my testimony that as we were going towards Konjevic Polje, as we moved, a megaphone was used from the APC that I was on. It was driven by Mirko Jankovic, and Mile Petrovic was there, too. And this megaphone was the property of UNPROFOR. And it was inside, as were other objects as part of the equipment of that armoured personnel carrier. And I claim that it was used and that Muslims were called with the megaphone from that APC to surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Petrovic also denies your version of the events, that is, that he took the six -- five or six prisoners and killed them, as you have described it. I take it you disagree with his account, his denial?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said precisely what happened in my statement and what my knowledge about it is. In my statement, I did not claim that Mile Petrovic, that I saw what Mile Petrovic did to them. I said how I saw that incident and what I was told so that I never claimed that I saw him kill them, and I stand by that. I didn't personally see Mile Petrovic killing them. But I said what Mile Petrovic told me when he came back, and I stand by that statement to this day. That is what I heard and what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you had asked your lawyers, in particular, Mr. Londrovic, to go and see if Mr. Petrovic could provide a statement to assist you with respect to who was ordering the military police. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't give such instructions to Mr. Londrovic. When we're talking about potential witnesses who were supposed to testify in these proceedings, I always gave him instructions and named people who might testify in a particular area. If he's a member of the police, then with reference to that area and within the framework of the indictment and the charges it contains against me. So those were the kinds of instructions I gave to my lawyers. It is quite normal that Mr. Londrovic was to have spoken to Mile Petrovic about the police and their involvement, how orders were issued, and things like that.
